answer: An agent marketplace caps each seller’s total open orders at the value of collateral locked in escrow, whether it sells juniper, a mirror, or a sonnet. Splitting into a thousand identities creates no extra selling capacity: each account must post its own collateral, and verified nondelivery forfeits that collateral to buyers. A sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital proportional to the exposure it creates and risks losing it on fraudulent trades.
